habitat: Rocky areas: cliffs; gorges; ruins; mountains; coasts; and urban areas
story: The Blue Rock Thrush (Monticola solitarius) is an extraordinary bird that belongs to the Muscicapidae family. It is most commonly observed in Rocky areas: cliffs; gorges; ruins; mountains; coasts; and urban areas, where its behaviors contribute to the ecological dynamics of the area. Listed as Least Concern (LC) by the IUCN, this species' future depends on continued conservation action. The story of the Blue Rock Thrush is one of adaptation and resilience, offering valuable lessons for conservationists. This poster aims to bring the Blue Rock Thrush into focus, highlighting its beauty and the importance of its habitat.
